processing_steps.method: casting in a 100 kW vacuum induction furnace
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Produced 0.5 kg ingots of the alloyed steel.
Ingots hot-rolled at 1150 °C to obtain 5 mm flat-products.
Hot-rolling was followed by water quenching.
Samples were heat treated at 800 °C for 30 min; tempering at 800 °C provided the maximum acceleration of reaction kinetics, allowing strong transformations even for short 30 min tempering.
Heat treatment at 800 °C was followed by water quenching.

structures.overall_structure: Cellular transformation for most of the austenite fraction plus spinodal decomposition for the remainder; the resulting microstructure is characterised by wide-spread κ + α + γ lamellar structures derived from cellular transformation, thin band-shaped δ-ferrite grains and scattered regions of spinodal decomposed γ; cellular-transformed fractions were predominant over the spinodal decomposed ones.

phases_present.morphology: detected as the portions of κ-carbide lamellae, suggesting a non-complete reaction

grain_structure.texture: equiaxed grains crossed by faint horizontal banded/lamellar features (optical micrograph of 800 °C-tempered 9Al-10Mn-1C)

microstructure_list.region: scattered regions of spinodal decomposed γ

phases_present.morphology: thin acicular, agglomerated into a relatively medium-dense grid

interfaces.phase_evolution: γ → κ + α + residual-γ lamellar structure (cellular transformation) and γ → γ0 + nano-sized κ-carbides (spinodal decomposition); both reactions occurred at 800 °C with the cellular product predominant over the spinodal product.
interfaces.interface_notes: For 9Al-10Mn-1C at 800 °C, cellular transformation generated κ + α + residual-γ lamellar phases (Fig. 6, Table 6); the residual austenite was detected as portions of κ-carbide lamellae, suggesting a non-complete reaction.

characterization_methods.key_findings: Table 6 (EDS for Al and Mn in 9Al-10Mn-1C tempered at 800 °C), wt% (Min/Mean/Max) — Al: δ 8.1/8.4/8.7, γ 6.8/7.4/8.7, k 8.6/9.4/10.0; Mn: δ 7.4/8.3/9.1, γ 11.1/11.4/12.3, k 10.1/12.3/13.8. Al is slightly enriched in the k phase and depleted in γ; Mn is strongly depleted in δ and enriched in γ and k. Nano-sized acicular κ-carbides observed in the spinodal-decomposed regions.

characterization_methods.technique: CALPHAD equilibrium phase volume fraction diagrams (Amount of all phases [mol] vs Temperature [°C])
characterization_methods.purpose: evaluate thermodynamic gradients for austenite stability and explain tempering-induced austenite decomposition
characterization_methods.key_findings: For 9Al-10Mn-1C the phase fraction diagram (Fig. 9(b)) shows BCC_A2 ~0.80 mol to ~650 °C then collapse near 800 °C; FCC_A1 climbs to ~1.00 mol at ~1000 °C; KAPPA_E21 ~0.20 mol below 600 °C and zero by ~950 °C; the γ fraction gradient detected between 600 °C and 800 °C.

computational_details.simulation_method: CALPHAD thermodynamic equilibrium calculation / phase volume fraction diagram
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The calculated γ fraction gradient was used as a qualitative indication of possible austenite transformation and compared with the observed microstructures at 600 °C and 800 °C.

analytical_models.model_note: FIG. 9(b): phase volume fraction diagram for 9Al-10Mn-1C, illustrating the thermodynamic gradient in austenite stability that the text ties to tempering-induced decomposition at 600 °C and 800 °C.

unmapped_findings: For 9Al-10Mn-1C annealed at 800 °C, the austenite decomposed such that cellular transformation governed most of the austenite fraction while spinodal decomposition governed the remainder; the residual austenite was detected as portions of κ-carbide lamellae, suggesting a non-complete reaction.

Tempering at 800 °C provided the maximum acceleration of the reaction kinetics, allowing strong transformations even for short 30 min tempering; this benefited from a medium-high Al–C driving force and medium-low austenite stability.

At 800 °C the 9Al-10Mn-1C alloy cell/colony structure resolved in SEM (Fig. 6) shows fields of fine parallel striations (cellular product) meeting smoother darker regions (spinodal product), with a lamellar spacing well below 1 µm (X10,000 panel, 1 µm scale bar).

Cellular-transformed fractions were predominant over spinodal-decomposed ones at 9Al-10Mn-1C (Fig. 13(a)) due to lower Mn% austenite stability; the 800 °C tempered 9Al-10Mn-1C microstructure is described as the best among alloys featuring 9% aluminium.
